- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >+2% per day) after a spike, it often overshoots; cap upward momentum at 1–2% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5), model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply a “reversion buffer” — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day after peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period spikes (especially >90) — add 1–2% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish or volatility is rising.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.5, -0.5, 0.0), model often fails to recognize the pattern — apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per negative sentiment day.
